title: Wednesday's boring SaaS, 14 October 2026
dek: Wednesday, 14 October 2026. Eight are Stripe-verified. SyncSignature and SendToDrive run on Paddle. Guidanz's Stripe key expired in August.

companies.name: Guidanz
companies.description: Two old-school B2B products from a US company founded in 2019 (TrustMRR). BI Connector links Oracle Fusion (ERP, HCM, SCM, CX), OTBI analyses and BI Publisher models straight into Power BI, Tableau or a warehouse, with no code. Skedler schedules and emails PDF, Excel, CSV and PNG reports from Grafana, Kibana, Wazuh and LogRhythm. Customers pay an annual subscription licence (company-stated). The site says "Profitable since day one" and "Trusted by Fortune 1000 companies" (company-stated).
companies.evidence: Last 12 months ~$255,093, last 6 months ~$90,166, last 3 months ~$15,998, all-time ~$1,447,862. MRR snapshot ~$1,291, 3 active subscriptions, 65% L30 profit margin (snapshot). Annual licences make monthly cash lumpy. L30 shows $0 only because syncing stopped. Last synced 27 Aug 2026 ~07:24 Warsaw; the Stripe API key expired that day, so figures are stale.
companies.indieAngle: Pick one legacy enterprise system with a weak reporting layer (Oracle Fusion, SAP B1, Sage X3, NetSuite) and sell the pipe into Power BI. Charge annually.
companies.whyItPrints: Oracle Fusion shops are stuck with OTBI, and their analysts live in Power BI. A connector that removes an IT ticket queue sells to enterprises on annual contracts with little churn.

companies.name: Astonish Email
companies.description: Plain newsletter and email-marketing tool for UK organisations: build from a template, schedule the send, pay for what you send, and talk to a person when you need one (company-stated). Plans start at £25/month (company-stated). ~2,000 users (founder-stated). TrustMRR lists it as founded Jul 2013 and the site says since 2012.
companies.evidence: ~$2,904 MRR, 16 active subscriptions, ~$2,620 L30, ~$31,526 last 12 months, ~$413,550 all-time. Only 16 subs against ~$2.6k/mo cash suggests a lot of pay-as-you-send credit revenue outside subscriptions. Revenue synced Oct 14, 2026 ~04:15 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Choose one country and one boring audience (charities, councils, schools), add human support, and charge for sends instead of seats.
companies.whyItPrints: A Mailchimp alternative for organisations that hate Mailchimp. The edge is UK billing, a human on support, and pay-per-send pricing. Thirteen years of quiet compounding.

companies.name: Paso Robles Wineries
companies.description: A WordPress guide to Paso Robles (California) wineries, tasting rooms, tours, lodging and dining. Running since at least 2017, one person (founder-stated). The founder describes a dominant SEO position, recurring revenue with annual contracts, and 90k+ social followers. Target: wine enthusiasts and local business owners. The profile does not spell out the product; the inference is that local businesses pay for listings or promotion.
companies.evidence: ~$4,695 MRR, 33 active subscriptions, ~$6,718 L30 (+37%), ~$55,880 last 12 months, ~$111,019 all-time. 9,049 visitors L30 (TrustMRR snapshot), about $0.74 revenue/visitor. Revenue synced Oct 14, 2026 ~08:16 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: One region, one tourism vertical, and an SEO moat. Sell annual listings to local businesses. Replicate it per region.
companies.whyItPrints: A local directory. Own the Google results for one tourist region and sell annual visibility to the wineries that need visitors.

companies.name: SyncSignature
companies.description: Free email-signature generator plus central management for Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail. Founded Nov 2023 in India, team of 2–5. Pricing (company-stated): Free, Solo $6/mo, Teams $2/user/mo (5-seat minimum), custom agency pricing. 40,000+ professionals (company-stated). Growth from SEO, content and the blog. DR 46.
companies.evidence: ~$2,556 MRR, 134 active subscriptions, ~$3,789 L30 (+108%), ~$33,739 last 12 months, ~$39,088 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 14, 2026 ~06:17 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Give away a free generator for SEO and charge for the per-seat admin panel. Same play as Exclaimer and WiseStamp, at indie prices.
companies.whyItPrints: Every company wants consistent signatures and nobody wants to build it in-house. The free generator pulls in SEO traffic, and per-seat team plans turn that into revenue.

companies.name: Check Position
companies.description: Simple daily Google position tracking across multiple datacenters. Pricing (company-stated): 7 keywords free, €15/month or €162/year. Listed for sale at $20,000 (2.8×), with 18 offers and 2,145 interested-buyer views (TrustMRR).
companies.evidence: ~$1,807 MRR, 235 active subscriptions, 60% L30 margin (snapshot), ~$601 L30 (−46%; annual renewals are lumpy), ~$38,277 last 12 months, ~$209,829 all-time. The trend is downward (L6M $13.5k vs L12M $38.3k), which is probably why it is for sale. Revenue synced Oct 14, 2026 ~04:43 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: A cheap acquisition target. About $38k a year verified against a $20k ask, if the decline can be stopped with SERP-API cost control and annual-plan pushes.
companies.whyItPrints: Rank tracking is a commodity and SEO people still pay for a cheap one. 235 subscribers on cheap plans add up to a long tail.

companies.name: AutoPrintEmail
companies.description: Standalone desktop app (Windows/Mac/Linux) that connects to Gmail, Outlook or IMAP and automatically prints new emails and attachments. No plugins. Founded Dec 2025 (AE). Pricing (company-stated): 3-day trial, then $29/month or $499 one-time per computer. Target (founder-stated): pharmacies, retailers, restaurants, warehouses, trades. They also promote a Shopify order-printing version.
companies.evidence: ~$1,739 L30 (+19%), last 12 months / all-time ~$24,299 (about 10 months old). MRR ~$425, 29 active subscriptions. Most revenue appears to be the $499 one-time licences. Revenue synced Oct 14, 2026 ~04:30 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Sell the bridge from cloud inbox to physical printer to unglamorous SMBs. Add one-time licences to pull cash forward.
companies.whyItPrints: Back offices still run on paper: order tickets, prescriptions, pick lists. Paying monthly per printer PC is an easy yes, and lifetime licences bring in cash up front.

companies.name: SendToDrive
companies.description: A public upload page that drops files straight into a chosen Google Drive folder. Uploaders do not need a Google login, and you do not share Drive access. Used for client docs, assignments, event photos. Pricing (company-stated): 24h trial, Premium €3.96 billed annually, Business $9.99/workspace/month. Founded Jul 2023 (US).
companies.evidence: ~$1,518 MRR, 314 active subscriptions, ~$1,871 L30, ~$9,529 last 12 months, ~$9,854 all-time. 4,668 visitors L30, about $0.40/visitor (snapshot). Revenue synced Oct 14, 2026 ~06:50 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Find a missing feature in Google Workspace, Dropbox or OneDrive and ship it as a tiny paid wrapper with SEO landing pages.
companies.whyItPrints: Google never shipped a proper file request for consumer Drive. A thin wrapper fills that gap and claims 95% profit margin (TrustMRR snapshot).

companies.name: Whois JSON API
companies.description: REST API for structured WHOIS and RDAP, live DNS, bulk lookups, domain availability and change monitoring. Founded Nov 2021. Pricing (company-stated): Basic $49/mo, Premium $129/mo, Enterprise $299/mo.
companies.evidence: ~$1,196 MRR, 23 active subscriptions, ~$2,308 L30 (+53%), ~$17,501 last 12 months, ~$46,854 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 14, 2026 ~05:02 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Take one messy public data source, normalise it into JSON and charge a monthly plan. Feeds that need monitoring keep customers subscribed.
companies.whyItPrints: Security, brand-protection and domain-investor tools all need WHOIS, and the raw data is messy. Normalising it once and reselling it is plumbing.

companies.name: MON RDV PREFECTURE
companies.description: Watches French prefecture booking systems and sends real-time alerts when slots open (residence permits, naturalisation, and similar). €19.99/month (company-stated). ~12,207 users (founder-stated). Founded Aug 2022. Listed for sale at $65,000 (7.7×), 1 offer (TrustMRR).
companies.evidence: ~$672 MRR, 30 active subscriptions, ~$703 L30, ~$10,140 last 12 months, ~$21,324 all-time. The asking multiple is steep for about $10k a year. Revenue synced Oct 14, 2026 ~04:57 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Build a slot-alert service for a government booking system that is always full (consulates, driving tests, visa centres).
companies.whyItPrints: French bureaucracy keeps slots scarce, and people pay monthly to avoid refreshing a page at dawn. Very cheap to run: 98% L30 margin (snapshot).

companies.name: Country-specific job board
companies.description: A 15-year-old job board for one country (country not disclosed). Solo founder, bootstrapped, SEO-only acquisition (TrustMRR profile). Employers pay to post.
companies.evidence: ~$14,251 L30 (+145%), ~$78,799 last 12 months, ~$4,460 MRR, 17 active subscriptions, 70% L30 margin (snapshot), all-time on TrustMRR ~$79,346 (only since Stripe was connected; the business is older). Revenue synced Oct 14, 2026 ~08:50 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Niche or country job boards are still a cash business. Buy an aged one, or pick a country or profession that LinkedIn underserves.
companies.whyItPrints: An old domain with SEO equity brings in 309,636 visitors in 30 days (TrustMRR snapshot) without paid ads.

honorableMentions.name: Factura
honorableMentions.note: Swiss QR-invoice, expenses and time tracking for freelancers, 9 CHF/mo (company-stated). Stripe-verified ~$268 MRR, 25 subs, L30 ~$600, all-time ~$2,683.

honorableMentions.name: Ton-piston
honorableMentions.note: French internship and apprenticeship search with a Pro plan at €9.99/mo (company-stated). Stripe-verified ~$9,787 MRR, 933 subs, L30 ~$10,488 within about 2 months. AI-CV heavy.
